raw_segments.text: These pictures were in watercolors. The first represented clouds low and livid, rolling
over a swollen sea. All the distance was in eclipse, so, too, was the foreground, or rather,
the nearest billows, for there was no land. One gleam of light lifted into relief a half-submerged
mast, on which sat a cormorant, dark and large, with wings flecked with foam. Its beak held
a gold bracelet set with gems, that I had touched with as brilliant tints as my palate
could yield, and as glittering distinctness as my pencil could impart. Sinking below the
bird and mast, a drowned corpse glanced through the green water. A fair arm was the only limb
clearly visible, whence the bracelet had been washed or torn.
